newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes lower in weather market.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes lower in weather market.

text.p: Hopes for better spring wheat seeding weather soon in the U.S., a forecast for rain in France and an outlook for cool and damp weather in the U.S. Great Plains pressured MGE spring wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
"It was very, very limited volume. They're going to start planting in North Dakota this week, not in the flood areas, but they'll start to plant in Minnesota too," a trader said.
Flooding has delayed spring fieldwork including spring wheat seeding in the Dakotas and Minnesota but outlooks for better wheat seeding weather were noted.
Wheat also was hit by an outlook for rain in France and on ideas crop loss estimates in the U.S. Great Plains may be exaggerated, traders said.

There were outlooks for light rain in France by the weekend which could stem further declines in production prospects for the French wheat crop. But a spokesperson for the French ACPA farm lobby said the dry and cold weather already has done some serious damage in France and experts now predict possible yield losses of 10 to 20 percent for winter grains.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 24.127 million bushels, below the 30.350 million traded Tuesday.
MGE spring wheat futures closed 10 to 12-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with May down 11 at $4.54-1/4. July was down 12-1/2 cents at $4.54-1/2.
Barley futures closed unchanged to 0.20 cents per cwt higher, with May up 0.20 at $6.85 per cwt.
